html:
The Wadikali were an Aboriginal Australian people of the far northwest corner of New South Wales, near the borders with South Australia and Queensland. Their speech was one of the Yarli dialects, shared with the Malyangapa and the Yardliyawara.

Little more is recorded. Neighbours included the Pirlatapa, the Karenggapa and the Yandruwandha of Cooper Creek. In 1845 Charles Sturt's expedition was stranded for six months at Depot Glen near today's Milparinka, close to this country, waiting for rain. Sheep stations and small goldfields followed in later decades.
